rationale: Low-capital, license-free and paid on delivery, but retailers give sampling away to win fertilizer sales, the fall window is short, and fields repeat only every 2-4 years. rationale: Seed is a mandatory annual input, but dealer commissions are missing entirely, appointments are controlled by seed companies favoring farmer-dealers, and sales run on multi-year personal relationships a non-farmer outsider lacks. Extreme township-level competition and no wedge. Low capital does not offset low probability of meaningful profit.

Only farm-count data supports this; dealer margins, territory availability and transaction sizes are all assumed. Hardware margins are thin, demo inventory ties up cash, OEM dealership precision departments dominate, and farm capex is cyclical. In-season service reputation can build a regional book, but an outsider without ag credibility starts far behind.

Genuine safety-driven need and paid-on-completion, but no pricing or frequency data; demand is a short pre-harvest window and many farmers self-perform. Engulfment and dust-explosion liability make insurance a likely margin killer. Local seasonal crew business with a low ceiling; robot-assisted angle is a modest wedge.

5-15% buy-sell margins on inventory plus 6-12 months of grower credit, against co-ops bundling agronomy, credit and rebates. Record itself admits no credible small-scale entry strategy. Launch capital $100-500k breaches the capital gate, hazmat storage and pesticide dealer licensing add burden. Consumable demand is the only positive.
